Rashi on Sukkah 20b:10:1.hebrew: הישן לא יצא - דאהל מפסיק בינו לסוכה, ועיקר ישיבת הסוכה — אכילה, שתיה ושינה:
Rashi on Sukkah 20b:10:1.english: One who sleeps did not fulfill [his obligation] - For a tent intervenes between him and the sukkah, and the essence of dwelling in the sukkah is eating, drinking, and sleeping.

Rashi on Sukkah 20b:10:2.hebrew: נוהגין היינו כו' - טעמא מפרש בגמרא, דלא אתי אהל עראי ומבטל אהל קבע:
Rashi on Sukkah 20b:10:2.english: It was our custom, etc. - The reason is explained in the Gemara: that a temporary tent does not come and nullify a permanent tent.

Rashi on Sukkah 20b:11:1.hebrew: מעשה בטבי עבדו - ועבדים פטורין מן הסוכה, דמצות עשה שהזמן גרמא נשים פטורות, וכל שהאשה חייבת — עבד נמי חייב, כדאמרי' בחגיגה (דף ד.):
Rashi on Sukkah 20b:11:1.english: An incident involving Tavi his slave - And slaves are exempt from the sukka, as women are exempt from positive, time-bound commandments, and whatever a woman is obligated in, a slave is also obligated in, as we say in Chagigah (4a):

Rashi on Sukkah 20b:11:2.hebrew: ולפי דרכינו למדנו - כלומר, אע"פ שלא אמר לנו לשם לימוד, אלא לשיחת חולין בעלמא — שהיה משתבח בעבדו לבדיחותא בעלמא — למדנו ע"פ דרך בדיחותו, שהישן תחת המטה לא יצא ידי חובתו:
Rashi on Sukkah 20b:11:2.english: And by the way we learned - That is to say, even though he did not say [this] to us for the sake of instruction, but merely as casual conversation — in that he was praising his servant merely in jest — we learned by way of his jest that one who sleeps beneath the bed did not fulfill his obligation.

Rashi on Sukkah 20b:13:1.english: We learned there - In [tractate] Ohalot, [the Mishnah] enumerates those that bring impurity.

Rashi on Sukkah 20b:13:2.hebrew: שחררוהו המים - כגון בשפה גבוהה על הנהר, והמים חוטטין מתחתיה ונכנסין ועושין נקב ארוך:
Rashi on Sukkah 20b:13:2.english: That the water hollowed it out - For example, in a high bank above a river, where the water hollows out beneath it and enters, making a long cavity.

Rashi on Sukkah 20b:13:3.english: Or creeping animals - Such as weasels and moles.

Rashi on Sukkah 20b:13:4.english: Or that saltiness ate it away - That the ground is salty and splits open on its own.

Rashi on Sukkah 20b:13:5.hebrew: וכן מדבך - אבנים גדולות הערוכות זו על זו. ופעמים שהאחת סדורה על גבי השנים, והתחתונות שוכבות זו אצל זו ומפרידות זו מזו, ויש שם אהל טפח:
Rashi on Sukkah 20b:13:5.english: And likewise a course - Large stones arranged one upon the other. And sometimes, one is arranged on top of two, and the lower ones lie next to each other and are separated from each other, and there is a tent of a handbreadth there.

Rashi on Sukkah 20b:13:6.hebrew: וכן סואר של קורות - אף הן קורות הערוכות על גבי קרקע, זו על גב זו, ועומדות לבנין, ויש שם הרבה נקבים ביניהם ויש בהן אהל. כל אלו — אם כזית מת בתוך האהל בראשו אחד וכלים בראשו שני, נטמאו באהל המת:
Rashi on Sukkah 20b:13:6.english: And likewise, a pile of beams - These too are beams arranged on the ground, one on top of the other, and designated for construction, and there are many cavities between them and they contain [the space of] a tent. [Regarding] all of these: if an olive-bulk of a corpse is inside the tent at one end of it and vessels are at its other end, they become impure through the tent over the corpse.

Rashi on Sukkah 20b:14:1.english: By human hands - [That one] intends to make it a tent.

Rashi on Sukkah 20b:14:2.english: Is not a tent - With regard to [ritual] impurity.

Rashi on Sukkah 20b:1:1.hebrew: שהן טמאות - אף מדרס, דמיוחדות לשכיבה הן ולא לתשמיש אחר:
Rashi on Sukkah 20b:1:1.english: That they are ritually impure - Even [with] midras [impurity], for they are designated for lying [upon] and not for another use.

Rashi on Sukkah 20b:1:2.hebrew: ועל של טבריא - קשות הן, ואין לך אדם שוכב עליהן:
Rashi on Sukkah 20b:1:2.english: And concerning [those] of Tiberias - They are stiff, and you have no person who lies upon them.

Rashi on Sukkah 20b:1:3.english: Since there is no one who sits on them - Most people are not accustomed to designate them for this [purpose].

Rashi on Sukkah 20b:1:4.english: That it happens and [one] sits - And [one] designates them for this [purpose].

Rashi on Sukkah 20b:2:2.hebrew: וכן היה ר' דוסא אומר כדבריו - של ר' יוסי, דזו וזו מסככין בה — אלמא, לאו כלי הוא לקבל טומאה:
Rashi on Sukkah 20b:2:2.english: And likewise Rabbi Dosa would say in accordance with his statement - [Of] Rabbi Yosei, that one may roof with both this [one] and that [one] — which shows that it is not a vessel [susceptible] to contract ritual impurity.

Rashi on Sukkah 20b:3:1.hebrew: גדנפא - כעין שפה סביב, גבוה מעט, לקבל מה שנותנין בהו, ועשויה לתשמיש — לתת פירות על גבה:
Rashi on Sukkah 20b:3:1.english: A rim - A sort of rim around [it], slightly raised, to retain what is placed in them, and [thus it is] made for use — to place fruit upon it.

Rashi on Sukkah 20b:3:2.hebrew: דלית ביה גדנפא - אפילו כלי לא הויא, דלסכך על גבי אהלים עשויה:
Rashi on Sukkah 20b:3:2.english: That does not have a rim - It is not even a vessel, as it is made to cover over tents.

Rashi on Sukkah 20b:4:1.english: Sha’am - [*Fueille* in Old French, meaning foliage], a type of shifah [bast].

Rashi on Sukkah 20b:4:3.english: Of sefira - From that which is sheared from the neck of a horse and from its tail.

Rashi on Sukkah 20b:4:4.hebrew: מטמאין טמא מת - ולא מדרס, דכלי הן ולא לישיבה:
Rashi on Sukkah 20b:4:4.english: They become ritually impure [with] corpse impurity - But not [with] midras [impurity], for they are vessels, but [are] not [designated] for sitting.

Rashi on Sukkah 20b:5:1.hebrew: בשלמא למאן דאמר - חוצלות היינו מזבלי, איכא למימר בכל הני: דכי לא עבידן לשכיבה, כלי הם לתשמיש אחר:
Rashi on Sukkah 20b:5:1.english: Granted, according to the one who said - [That] ḥotzalot are sacks [mazvelei], it can be said regarding all of these [materials] that when they are not made for lying upon, they are [nevertheless] a vessel for another use.

Rashi on Sukkah 20b:5:10.hebrew: למאי חזיין - אליבא דרבי דוסא, דאמר לאו לשכיבה עבידן, אמאי טמאות שום טומאה:
Rashi on Sukkah 20b:5:10.english: For what are they fit - According to Rabbi Dosa, who said [that] they are not made for lying upon, why are they susceptible to any impurity?

Rashi on Sukkah 20b:5:11.english: For vats - To cover with them a vat in which they make beer.

Rashi on Sukkah 20b:5:2.hebrew: של שעם ושל גמי - אף על פי שאין נארגים היטב, ויש הפרש בין בית ניר לבית ניר:
Rashi on Sukkah 20b:5:2.english: [Those] of papyrus and of bulrushes - Even though they are not woven tightly, and there is a gap between one heddle loop and another:

Rashi on Sukkah 20b:5:3.hebrew: ראויין הן לכנתא דפירי - פירות גסין, שאין יוצאין דרך נקב קטן:
Rashi on Sukkah 20b:5:3.english: They are fit for a fruit basket - [For] large fruits, which do not fall out through a small hole.

Rashi on Sukkah 20b:5:4.english: Of sackcloth and of horsehair - For they are woven finely.

Rashi on Sukkah 20b:5:5.hebrew: חזו לגולקי וצני - כלים כעין שקין, שנותנין בהן קטניות ופירות דקין:
Rashi on Sukkah 20b:5:5.english: [They are] fit for gulekei and tzannei - [These are] vessels like sacks, in which one places legumes and small fruits.

Rashi on Sukkah 20b:5:6.english: However, according to the one who said actual mats - For they are flat and have no receptacle.

Rashi on Sukkah 20b:5:7.hebrew: בשלמא של שק ושל ספירא - לר' דוסא, אע"ג דלאו לשכיבה עבידי:
Rashi on Sukkah 20b:5:7.english: Granted, [those] of sackcloth and of horsehair - [This is understandable] according to Rabbi Dosa, even though they are not made for lying [upon].

Rashi on Sukkah 20b:5:8.hebrew: חזו לפרסי ונפוותא - לוילון כנגד הפתח, כדמתרגם "מסך הפתח" (שמות לה) — "פרסא דתרעא":
Rashi on Sukkah 20b:5:8.english: They are fit for screens and sifters - For a curtain in front of the doorway, as [the Targum] translates "the screen of the doorway" (Exodus 35:15) — "the curtain of the doorway."

Rashi on Sukkah 20b:5:9.hebrew: נפוותא - לנפות בהן הקמח כמות שהן: נותנין עליו קמח, וכופלין אותן, וקושרין בראש הכפל, כעין בויטי"ל שלנו:
Rashi on Sukkah 20b:5:9.english: Sifters - To sift flour with them as they are: they place flour upon it, fold them, and tie at the top of the fold, like our boitel [flour sifter].

Rashi on Sukkah 20b:7:1.english: Ḥananya - [He was] the son of Rabbi Yehoshua's brother.

Rashi on Sukkah 20b:7:2.hebrew: כשירדתי לגולה - כשירד לגולה לעבר שנה, כדאמרינן בברכות בהרואה (ברכות דף סג.):
Rashi on Sukkah 20b:7:2.english: When I descended to the exile - When he descended to the exile to intercalate the year, as we say in Berakhot in [the chapter entitled] HaRo'eh (Berakhot 63a).

Rashi on Sukkah 20b:7:4.hebrew: מסככים - דסתמא לסיכוך, ואינה כלי לתשמיש:
Rashi on Sukkah 20b:7:4.english: One may roof - For ordinarily [it is made] for roofing, and it is not a utensil for [personal] use.

Rashi on Sukkah 20b:8:1.english: A wall - That is a rim [gedanfa].

Tosafot on Sukkah 20b:10:1.hebrew: הישן תחת המטה בסוכה לא יצא ידי חובתו - בגמרא מוקי לה שמואל בגבוהה עשרה, דפחות מכאן לא חשיב אהל להפסיק. ומצינן למימר דשמואל לטעמיה, דמכשר בפרק קמא (דף י.) תחתונה כשאין בעליונה עשרה. אבל לאינך אמוראי דפסלי, משום דעליונה חשיבא אהל אע"פ שאינה גבוהה י' — הוא הדין דחשיב אהל להפסיק? ושמא מטה שאני, כדאמר בגמרא דהויא לה מטה אהל עראי; הלכך כולהו מודו דבפחות מעשרה לאו כלום היא:
Tosafot on Sukkah 20b:10:1.english: One who sleeps beneath the bed in the sukkah did not fulfill his obligation - In the Gemara, Shmuel establishes [the Mishnah as referring to a bed that is] ten [handbreadths] high, because less than this is not considered a tent to form an intervening barrier. And we can say that Shmuel is consistent with his reasoning, as he validates [the lower sukkah] in the first chapter (10a) when the upper one does not have ten [handbreadths]. But according to the other Amoraim who invalidate [it] because the upper one is considered a tent even though it is not ten [handbreadths] high, does that same rule apply [here, that a bed is] considered a tent to form an intervening barrier? And perhaps a bed is different, as [the Gemara] says in the Gemara that a bed is a temporary tent; therefore, everyone agrees that with less than ten [handbreadths] it is nothing.

Tosafot on Sukkah 20b:11:1.hebrew: ראיתם טבי עבדי שהוא תלמיד חכם - עבד כשר היה, כדאיתא בפרק שני דברכות (דף טז:). ובירושלמי תני: שהיה מניח תפילין, ולא מיחו בידו חכמים. ופריך: מחלפא שיטתי' דרבן גמליאל — דהא הכא גבי סוכה מיחו בידו חכמים מלישב בסוכה, שהרי היה ישן תחת המטה! ומשני: שהיה עושה כן שלא לדחוק את חכמים שהיו ישנים בסוכה. ופריך: אי שלא לדחוק את חכמים, ישב לו חוץ לסוכה! ומשני: דרוצה היה לשמוע דברי חכמים:
Tosafot on Sukkah 20b:11:1.english: "Did you see my slave Tavi, who is a Torah scholar" - He was a virtuous slave, as is stated in the second chapter of Berakhot (16b). And in the Yerushalmi it is taught that he would wear tefillin, and the Sages did not protest against him. And [the Yerushalmi] asks: Is the position of Rabban Gamliel reversed? For behold, here regarding the sukkah, the Sages protested against his sitting in the sukkah, as he was sleeping beneath the bed! And [the Yerushalmi] answers: He was doing so in order not to crowd the Sages who were sleeping in the sukkah. And [the Yerushalmi] asks: If [it was] in order not to crowd the Sages, let him sit outside the sukkah! And [the Yerushalmi] answers: Because he wanted to hear the words of the Sages.

Tosafot on Sukkah 20b:13:1.hebrew: תנן התם - באהלות פ"ג [מ"ז]: "אחד חור שחררוהו מים" — ארישא קאי, דאיירי בביב שהוא קמור תחת הבית; וקמ"ל, אע"פ שנעשה ע"י מים או שרצים:
Tosafot on Sukkah 20b:13:1.english: "We learned there" - In Oholot, chapter 3 [Mishnah 7]: "Whether a hole that was perforated by water..." — [this] refers to the first clause [of the mishnah], which deals with a drain that is vaulted beneath the house; and it teaches us [that this applies] even though it was formed by water or creeping animals.

Tosafot on Sukkah 20b:5:1.hebrew: חזיין לפרסי - מסך לפני הפתח, ומקבל טומאה הוא, כדאמרי' סוף פרק קמא דביצה (דף יד: ושם): מפני מה אמרו וילון טמא:
Tosafot on Sukkah 20b:5:1.english: They are fit for screens - A screen in front of an entrance. And it is susceptible to ritual impurity, as we say [at the] end of the first chapter of Beitzah (14b and there): "For what reason did they say [that] a curtain is ritually impure?"

Tosafot on Sukkah 20b:5:2.hebrew: חזיין לנזייתא - פי' בקונטרס: לכסות בהן גיגית שעושין בה שכר. ואי אפשר לומר כן, דשעם וגמי לא מקבלי טומאה אלא מתורת כלי עץ, דאיתקש לשק. ובמסכת כלים פי"ו [מ"ח] תנן גבי כלי עור וכלי עץ: "זה הכלל: העשוי לתיק — טמא, ולחיפוי — טהור". ותנן נמי פכ"ו [מ"ו] במס' כלים: "עור שעשאו חיפוי לכלים — טהור". דהא דפליגי התם: "למשקולת — טמא, ורבי יוסי מטהר" — משום דהעשוי לכסות משקולת, פעמים שמקבלין בו דבר; ור' יוסי מטהר משום דעיקרו לכסוי. וצריך לומר הכא: שעושין לקבל בהן דבר:
Tosafot on Sukkah 20b:5:2.english: "They are fit for vats" - The Kuntres explained: To cover with them a vat in which they make beer. But it is impossible to say so, for [items of] papyrus and bulrush only contract ritual impurity under the category of wooden vessels, which are juxtaposed [in the Torah] to sackcloth. And in tractate Kelim, chapter 16 [mishnah 8], we learned regarding leather vessels and wooden vessels: "This is the general rule: That which is made as a case is ritually impure, but [that which is made] for covering is pure." And we also learned in chapter 26 [mishnah 6] of tractate Kelim: "A piece of leather that one made as a cover for vessels is pure." For this that they dispute there: "[Leather made to cover] a weight is ritually impure, and Rabbi Yose deems it pure" — [the first Tanna rules it impure] because that which is made to cover a weight, sometimes one places an item inside it; and Rabbi Yose deems it pure because its primary purpose is for covering. And [therefore] one must say here: that they make them to receive an item inside them.

Tosafot on Sukkah 20b:7:1.hebrew: מסככין בבודיא - עשויה היא לקבל תמרים, כדאשכחן בכתובות פרק נערה (כתובות דף נ:): "זיל הב ליה מתמרי דעל בודיא". וא"ת: אם כן, מקבלת טומאה מדרבנן כדף של נחתומין, פרק המוכר את הבית (ב"ב דף סו.), והיאך מסככין בה? ויש לומר: דההיא דאית ליה גדנפא היא העשויה לקבל תמרים, והך מוקמינן בדלית ליה גדנפא, דההיא ודאי עשויה לסיכוך וטהורה:
Tosafot on Sukkah 20b:7:1.english: One may roof with a mat - It is made to hold dates, as we find in Ketubot, in the chapter [entitled] Na'arah (Ketubot 50b): "Go give him from the dates that are upon the mat." And if you say: If so, it should be susceptible to ritual impurity by Rabbinic law like a baker's board, [as taught in] the chapter [entitled] Hamokher Et Habayit (Bava Batra 66a), and how [then] may one roof with it? And one can say: That [mat] which has a rim is the one that is made to hold dates, whereas this one [permitted here] we establish as [one] that does not have a rim, for that [kind] is certainly made for roofing and is pure.
